attributes.body_ja:
「遂（つい）に」は、「到頭（とうとう）」と同（おな）じように、「最終的（さいしゅうてき）に」という意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）す副詞（ふくし）です。基本的（きほんてき）に、文（ぶん）の頭（あたま）で使（つか）われます。

「遂（つい）に」はひらがなと漢字（かんじ）、どちらで書（か）かれることもあります。「到頭（とうとう）」と比（くら）べると、「ついに」の方（ほう）が少（すこ）しだけフォーマルな表現（ひょうげん）です。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

漢字（かんじ）の「遂（すい）」には、「最後（さいご）まで行（おこな）う」のような意味（いみ）がありますが、「ついに」は長（なが）い時間（じかん）や過程（かてい）のあとで起（お）こった出来事（できごと）に使（つか）われます。時間（じかん）や努力（どりょく）が必要（ひつよう）ない出来事（できごと）には使（つか）われません。
attributes.body:
Like とうとう, 遂（つい）に is an adverb that is frequently used to mean 'finally', or 'at last'. It will usually come at the beginning of a sentence.

遂（つい）に may be seen equally as often with or without kanji. When compared to 到頭（とうとう）, ついに is slightly more formal.

Caution

The kanji 遂（つい） has a meaning similar to 'to get (something) over with'. Due to this, ついに will most often be used to highlight things that have finally happened after a significant period of time, or a long course of events. It will not be used to express things that do not require time or effort.

attributes.description: Difference between いよいよ,やっと,とうとう,ようやく, and ついに

attributes.body: Both 遂に and いよいよ can mean 'finally', but with different focus. 遂に indicates that something has occurred at last, often after struggle or delay, e.g. '遂に大学に入った' ('I finally entered university'). いよいよ emphasizes an approaching climax or moment of anticipation, e.g. 'いよいよ卒業の日が来た' ('Graduation day has finally arrived').

second_relatable.title: いよいよ
second_relatable.meaning: At last, Finally, More and more

attributes.body: Both とうとう and 遂に mean 'finally', but with different nuances. とうとう emphasizes the long effort or struggle leading up to the result, while 遂に focuses more on the result itself and what may follow. In other words, both とうとう大学生になった and 遂に大学生になった mean 'I finally became a university student.', but the former is more backward-looking, while the latter is forward-looking.
